feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
OP_CODESEPARATOR's implementation within Bitcoin Script is under discussion, particularly regarding its semantics and how it should be handled in future versions. An ideal approach would involve signing the position of the last executed OP_CODESEPARATOR, which offers a more precise and robust realization of its intended functionality. This method enhances clarity in the script's execution semantics and ensures consistency during transaction verification.
However, there are practical considerations that necessitate retaining the current, albeit awkward, implementation of OP_CODESEPARATOR, especially since legacy Pay-to-Script-Hash (P2SH) scripts may continue to rely on this opcode indefinitely. Altering its behavior or introducing significant changes could inadvertently impact consensus and risk breaking backward compatibility for existing scripts.
Maintaining the status quo for OP_CODESEPARATOR helps avoid needless complexity in the consensus codebase, which already contends with numerous flag combinations. Until a decisive move is made to isolate new Script versions by duplicating code rather than layering additional flags, preserving the legacy behavior remains the most stable path forward. This strategy mitigates the risk of accidental consensus changes and ensures the continued reliable functioning of legacy scripts.
